newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby Union-Australia's Smith loses Morgan, ponders future.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Australia's Smith loses Morgan, ponders future.

text.p: Australia rugby union coach Greg Smith said on Friday his future in the job could depend on a victory over South Africa in this weekend's Tri-Nations match.
Reeling from successive heavy defeats against competition leaders New Zealand, Smith has faced increasing criticism in recent weeks over his tactics and failure to find a settled Wallaby line-up.

"(Saturday) night's test against the South Africans at Suncorp Stadium could well be a determining factor in whether I'm still Australian coach next year," Smith wrote in a Sydney newspaper column on Friday.
"I'm under a lot of pressure," Smith said. "Sometimes I wake up in the night and it's on my mind and I have trouble getting back to sleep."
Australia suffered a blow on Friday when lock Garrick Morgan was ruled out because of a shoulder injury sustained in training earlier in the week. His place was taken by Owen Finegan.

Smith, whose second one-year contract expires at the end of 1997, defended his record this season in tests not involving the All Blacks, who lead the Tri-Nations competition after beating South Africa and Australia away in the past fortnight.
In three earlier tests at home this season, Australia twice defeated Five Nations champions France and Triple Crown winners England once to compensate for those losses to New Zealand.

"If we beat the Springboks, we get to a 4-2 situation, with wins over three of the four teams who were rated above us after the 1995 World Cup," said Smith, referring to his win-loss record this season.

"I don't think there is anything wrong with that record in international rugby, but maybe I'm having myself on," wrote Smith, who took over from Bob Dwyer after Australia's surprise quarter-final World Cup exit two years ago.

"We're improving all the time as we move towards the 1999 World Cup. In fact, we've climbed from fifth (in the world rankings) at best and could reach number two if we topple South Africa," Smith wrote.

Former Wallaby flanker Simon Poidevin this week criticised Smith's tactics as outdated and confused, saying Australia played like a club side in their 33-18 defeat against New Zealand in a Tri-Nations match in Melbourne on Saturday.
Other commentators have lamented the constant team changes as Smith has searched for an effective scrum and back line combination.
Of the forwards, for example, only captain and lock John Eales has been a constant fixture this season.

Australia overhauled their back row again when they recalled flankers David Wilson and Matt Cockbain and switched breakaway Daniel Manu to number eight. Morgan's late withdrawal added to the upheavals.
Veteran fly-half David Knox also came into the side to replace injured Tim Horan.
The Springboks made only one change to the side that lost 35-32 to the All Blacks in the series opener on July 19, naming prop Dawie Theron to replace Marius Hurter.

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson, 6-Matt Cockbain, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Heath, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt. REUTER
